name: Retail Marketing & Digital Funnel
description: Date x Traffic Source acquisition and daily digital conversion. The only view of demand before it becomes a transaction. KNOWN LIMIT, BY DESIGN: no order in this dataset carries a traffic source, so per-source ROAS is not derivable - spend and visits are modelled per source, revenue only per day and explicitly blended. Sources conformed dimensions from the Retail Sales Activity model.

elements.name: SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC
elements.description: Daily web sessions by acquisition source. 9,132 rows = 1,522 days x 6 sources, exactly co-grained with F_MARKETING_SPEND.

elements.name: SRC F_MARKETING_SPEND
elements.description: Daily media spend by source. Same 9,132 keys as F_WEB_TRAFFIC, so the two join 1:1 with no orphans on either side.

elements.name: SRC Date
elements.description: Conformed Date dimension (4-5-4 fiscal) referenced from the Retail Sales Activity model.

elements.name: SRC Promotion
elements.description: 52 promotions with start/end dates, referenced from the Retail Sales Activity model.

elements.name: SRC Markdowns
elements.description: Product price-change ledger referenced from the Retail Sales Activity model.

elements.name: SRC Sales Activity
elements.description: Sales + returns fact referenced from the Retail Sales Activity model, projected to the columns needed for daily digital revenue.

elements.name: Date
elements.description: Retail 4-5-4 fiscal calendar. Sigma's built-in period-over-period and DateLookback are CALENDAR-based and will not align to 4-5-4 week boundaries; use Prior Year Date for fiscal-correct comps. Wider than the funnel window (web traffic runs 2021-08-19 to 2025-10-18).

elements.name: Traffic Source
elements.description: The six web acquisition sources. Direct and Organic Search carry ZERO spend on all 1,522 days - they are free traffic and together supply 2,148,437 visits (44.4% of all sessions). Any cost-per-visit or ROAS figure that averages them in with paid media is diluted by design; slice by Is Paid Source or Source Group to avoid it.

columns.name: Is Paid Source
columns.formula: If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Paid Search" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Social" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Email" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Referral", True, False)
columns.description: True for Paid Search, Social, Email and Referral, all of which record spend on every day. False for Direct and Organic Search, which record $0 on every day.

columns.name: Source Group
columns.formula: If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Paid Search" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Social", "Paid Media", If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Email" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Referral", "Owned & Earned", "Free"))
columns.description: Paid Media (Paid Search, Social - $1.50M of the $1.56M total spend), Owned & Earned (Email, Referral), Free (Direct, Organic Search).

columns.name: Lifetime Visits
columns.description: All-time sessions from this source, for sizing only.

elements.name: Promotion
elements.description: 52 promotions: 37 Seasonal, 15 Flash Sale; 40 tagged Channel = All and 12 Web-only. Discounts run 10-34%. They cover 288 of the 1,522 funnel days and overlap two-deep on 16 of those days - which is why Promo Day rolls promotions up to one row per date before they reach any fact.

elements.name: Web Daily
elements.description: F_WEB_TRAFFIC and F_MARKETING_SPEND collapsed from Date x Source to one row per date, carrying the paid/free split that the day grain would otherwise lose.

columns.name: Paid Visits
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Paid Search" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Social" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Email" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Referral", [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Web Visits], 0))

columns.name: Free Visits
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Paid Search" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Social" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Email" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Referral", 0, [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Web Visits]))
columns.description: Direct + Organic Search sessions - 44.4% of all traffic, acquired at zero recorded cost.

columns.name: Paid Media Spend
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Paid Search" or [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Social", [SRC F_MARKETING_SPEND/Spend], 0))
columns.description: Paid Search + Social only.

columns.name: Paid Search Visits
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Paid Search", [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Web Visits], 0))

columns.name: Organic Visits
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Traffic Source] = "Organic Search", [SRC F_WEB_TRAFFIC/Web Visits], 0))

elements.name: Digital Daily
elements.description: Sales Activity collapsed to one row per SALE DATE. MANDATORY pre-aggregation - joining line-grain Sales Activity to a day spine would fan the funnel out 4.9M ways. Dated by Sale Date, not Activity Date, so a return lands on the day of the order that produced it: revenue and returns on a given day are one cohort, which is what a spend-driven ROAS needs. All-time totals still tie exactly to the Retail Sales Activity model; only the day-by-day distribution of returns differs.

columns.name: Digital Gross Sales
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Sale" and [SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", [SRC Sales Activity/Amount], 0))
columns.description: Web + BOPIS + BOSS gross sales for orders placed this day.

columns.name: Digital Returns
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Return" and [SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", -[SRC Sales Activity/Amount], 0))
columns.description: Refunds against digital orders placed this day, whenever the refund was actually processed.

columns.name: Digital Net Sales
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", [SRC Sales Activity/Amount], 0))
columns.description: Digital gross sales less cohort returns.

columns.name: Digital Cost
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", [SRC Sales Activity/Cost], 0))

columns.name: Digital Units
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", [SRC Sales Activity/Quantity], 0))

columns.name: Web Gross Sales
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Sale" and [SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] = "Web", [SRC Sales Activity/Amount], 0))
columns.description: Pure-play Web channel only, excluding BOPIS and BOSS.

columns.name: Total Gross Sales
columns.formula: Sum(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Sale", [SRC Sales Activity/Amount], 0))
columns.description: All channels including Retail. Present only as the denominator for Digital Mix %.

columns.name: Digital Orders
columns.formula: CountDistinct(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Sale" and [SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", [SRC Sales Activity/Order Number], Null))
columns.description: Distinct Web + BOPIS + BOSS orders placed this day.

columns.name: Web Orders
columns.formula: CountDistinct(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Sale" and [SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] = "Web", [SRC Sales Activity/Order Number], Null))
columns.description: Distinct pure-play Web orders placed this day. This is the numerator behind the 2.54% baseline web conversion rate.

columns.name: Digital Customers
columns.formula: CountDistinct(If([SRC Sales Activity/Activity Type] = "Sale" and [SRC Sales Activity/Channel Type] <> "Retail", [SRC Sales Activity/Cust Key], Null))

elements.name: Promo Day
elements.description: Promotions exploded onto the calendar by a RANGE join (Date Key between Start Date and End Date), then collapsed to one row per date. The collapse is mandatory: 16 dates have two promotions running at once, so joining Promotion straight onto a day-grain fact would double those days' visits, spend and revenue.

columns.name: Active Promotions
columns.description: 0, 1 or 2. Two promotions overlap on 16 of the 288 promotional days.

columns.name: Max Discount Percent
columns.description: Deepest discount advertised this day, 10-34%.

columns.name: Promotion Name
columns.description: The promotion running this day. On the 16 dates where Active Promotions = 2 this shows only one of them - check Active Promotions before reading it as the whole story.

columns.name: Promotion Type
columns.description: Flash Sale or Seasonal, with the same one-of-two caveat as Promotion Name.

columns.name: Promotion Channel
columns.description: All or Web.

elements.name: Markdown Day
elements.description: The product price-change ledger collapsed to one row per effective date. 6,051 rows across 1,490 dates, but only 1,118 are genuine markdowns: the other 4,933 carry Discount Percent = 0 and are price RESETS back to full price. Counting all 6,051 as markdowns overstates promotional pressure five-fold.

columns.name: Price Changes
columns.description: Every price change effective this day, markdowns and resets alike.

columns.name: Markdowns
columns.description: Price changes that actually cut price. Exactly the rows carrying a Promotion Key.

columns.name: Price Resets
columns.description: Returns to full price. 4,933 of the 6,051 ledger rows.

columns.name: Products Marked Down
columns.formula: CountDistinct(If([SRC Markdowns/Discount Percent] > 0, [SRC Markdowns/Product Key], Null))

elements.name: Funnel by Source
elements.description: One row per Date x Traffic Source (9,132 = 1,522 days x 6 sources). Visits and spend join 1:1 with no orphans on either side. THERE IS DELIBERATELY NO REVENUE, ORDER COUNT OR CONVERSION RATE ON THIS ELEMENT. Orders in this dataset carry no traffic source, so per-source attribution is not derivable; allocating day revenue across sources by visit share would look like attribution while being an assumption. Use this element for acquisition volume, spend and efficiency-to-visit; use Funnel Day for anything that touches revenue.

columns.name: Web Visits
columns.description: Sessions from this source on this day.

columns.name: Spend
columns.description: Media spend against this source on this day. Always $0 for Direct and Organic Search - free traffic, not missing data.

columns.name: Active Promotions
columns.description: Promotions running company-wide this day. Lets acquisition volume be sliced by promotional pressure.

metrics.name: Web Visits
metrics.description: Web sessions from this source on these days. 4,834,940 all-time across the six sources. This is the only volume measure in the model that is genuinely attributable to a source.

metrics.name: Spend
metrics.description: Media spend booked against this source. $1,564,043.87 all-time. Always $0 for Direct and Organic Search - those are free traffic, not missing data - so a total across all six sources is a paid-media total even though it looks like a total for everything.

metrics.name: Paid Visits
metrics.description: Sessions from the four sources that record spend (Paid Search, Social, Email, Referral). 2,686,503 all-time, 55.6% of traffic.

metrics.name: Free Visits
metrics.description: Sessions from Direct and Organic Search, which cost nothing on all 1,522 days. 2,148,437 all-time - 44.4% of all traffic arrives free.

metrics.name: Cost per Visit
metrics.description: Spend divided by ALL visits, paid and free together. $0.3235 all-time. Diluted by construction: 44.4% of the denominator cost nothing. Use Cost per Paid Visit to judge media efficiency, and this only when you deliberately want blended cost of all traffic.

metrics.name: Cost per Paid Visit
metrics.description: Spend divided by visits from spending sources only. $0.5822 all-time - about 1.8x the blended figure. This is the honest media efficiency number. Per source: Paid Search $1.0041, Social $0.3976, Referral $0.2022, Email $0.0301.

metrics.name: Paid Visit Share %
metrics.description: Share of sessions that came from a source with spend against it. 55.6% all-time. Falling share means growing free traffic, not falling media performance - read it alongside Spend.

elements.name: Funnel Day
elements.description: One row per date (1,522: 2021-08-19 to 2025-10-18). The only element in this model where demand meets revenue. Visits and spend are rolled up from all six sources; digital orders and dollars are LEFT JOINed from pre-aggregated Sales Activity and are BLENDED ACROSS SOURCES BY CONSTRUCTION - no order in this dataset carries a traffic source, so every conversion, ROAS and revenue-per-visit figure here is a day-level blend and must never be read as the performance of any one channel. Every digital order date has a matching traffic row, so there are zero orphans in either direction (one traffic day, with no digital order, is genuine).

columns.name: Web Visits
columns.description: All sessions this day, every source.

columns.name: Free Visits
columns.description: Direct + Organic Search - 44.4% of all sessions at zero recorded cost.

columns.name: Paid Media Spend
columns.description: Paid Search + Social.

columns.name: Web Orders
columns.description: Pure-play Web channel orders. Pairs with Web Visits for the 2.54% baseline conversion rate.

columns.name: Digital Orders
columns.description: Web + BOPIS + BOSS. All three are placed online (transaction location 9999) and so all three are outcomes of the same web sessions - 3.76% of visits, not 2.54%.

columns.name: Digital Gross Sales
columns.description: Web + BOPIS + BOSS gross sales for orders placed this day.

columns.name: Digital Returns
columns.description: Refunds against orders placed this day (cohort-dated, not refund-dated), so they line up with the spend that drove them.

columns.name: Digital Gross Margin
columns.formula: Coalesce([Digital Daily/Digital Net Sales], 0) - Coalesce([Digital Daily/Digital Cost], 0)

columns.name: Total Gross Sales
columns.description: All channels including in-store. Present only as the denominator for Digital Mix %.

columns.name: Has Promotion
columns.description: True on 288 of 1,522 days. Slicing this model by it shows promotional days converting at 3.79% vs 3.75% and generating 1.7% LESS revenue per day - the promotion calendar has no measurable lift in this dataset.

columns.name: Markdowns
columns.description: Genuine price cuts effective this day.

metrics.name: Web Visits
metrics.description: Web sessions this day, summed across all six sources. 4,834,940 all-time. The denominator for every conversion and per-visit metric on this element.

metrics.name: Paid Visits
metrics.description: Sessions from Paid Search, Social, Email and Referral. 2,686,503 all-time (55.6%).

metrics.name: Marketing Spend
metrics.description: Total media spend this day. $1,564,043.87 all-time - only 0.53% of digital revenue, which is why every ROAS metric here reads implausibly high. See Blended ROAS.

metrics.name: Paid Media Spend
metrics.description: Paid Search + Social only. $1,501,129.55 all-time, 96.0% of total spend. Excludes Email and Referral, which record spend but behave as owned/earned channels.

metrics.name: Cost per Visit
metrics.description: Marketing Spend divided by Web Visits. $0.3235 all-time. Blended across paid and free traffic - for media efficiency use Cost per Paid Visit on Funnel by Source instead.

metrics.name: Web Orders
metrics.description: Distinct orders on the pure-play Web channel, excluding BOPIS and BOSS. 122,713 all-time. Numerator of the published 2.54% baseline conversion rate.

metrics.name: Digital Orders
metrics.description: Distinct Web + BOPIS + BOSS orders. 181,682 all-time. All three transact at location 9999, so all three are outcomes of the same web sessions - this, not Web Orders, is the true funnel outcome.

metrics.name: Web Conversion Rate %
metrics.description: Web Orders / Web Visits. 2.5380% all-time. This is the roadmap's published baseline, kept for continuity, but it understates the funnel by excluding BOPIS and BOSS. Prefer Digital Conversion Rate %.

metrics.name: Digital Conversion Rate %
metrics.description: Digital Orders / Web Visits. 3.7577% all-time - half again the web-only rate. The honest measure of what a web session is worth, because BOPIS and BOSS orders are placed online too. BLENDED ACROSS SOURCES: no order carries a traffic source, so this can never be split by channel.

metrics.name: Digital Gross Sales
metrics.description: Web + BOPIS + BOSS gross sales for orders PLACED this day. $297,012,840.24 all-time. Ties exactly to the Retail Sales Activity model.

metrics.name: Digital Returns
metrics.description: Refunds against digital orders placed this day, wherever the refund later landed (cohort-dated, not refund-dated), so returns face the spend that bought the revenue. $26,766,803.85 all-time - identical to Sales Activity; only the day-by-day distribution differs.

metrics.name: Digital Net Sales
metrics.description: Digital Gross Sales less cohort returns. $270,246,036.39 all-time.

metrics.name: Digital Return Rate %
metrics.description: Digital Returns / Digital Gross Sales. 9.01% all-time, against 5.44% company-wide and 4.23% in-store. Digital returns run more than 2x the in-store rate - the single largest cost of digital growth.

metrics.name: Digital Gross Margin
metrics.description: Digital Net Sales less digital cost of goods. $52,668,135.12 all-time. Struck AFTER returns, not before - the pre-returns figure is $57.9M, so returns cost roughly $5.2M of digital margin.

metrics.name: Digital Margin %
metrics.description: Digital Gross Margin / Digital Net Sales. 19.49% all-time.

metrics.name: Revenue per Visit
metrics.description: Digital Gross Sales / Web Visits. $61.43 all-time. The clearest single measure of session value, and the right yardstick for judging whether a traffic push paid off. Blended across sources by construction.

metrics.name: Digital AOV
metrics.description: Digital Gross Sales / Digital Orders. $1,634.80 all-time, effectively identical to the in-store basket ($1,645.25) - digital in this business is not a lower-value channel, only a higher-returning one.

metrics.name: Cost per Digital Order
metrics.description: Marketing Spend / Digital Orders. $8.61 all-time. An acquisition cost only in the loosest sense: 44.4% of traffic is free and no order is attributed to a source, so this is cost per order across all demand, not cost of a media-acquired order.

metrics.name: Blended ROAS
metrics.description: Digital Gross Sales / Marketing Spend. 189.90x all-time. DO NOT PLAN AGAINST THIS. Recorded spend is 0.53% of digital revenue, a property of the dataset rather than a business result, and the revenue is blended across paid and free traffic. Retained for completeness; use Cost per Visit and Revenue per Visit for real decisions.

metrics.name: Blended Net ROAS
metrics.description: Digital Net Sales / Marketing Spend. 172.79x all-time. Same caveat as Blended ROAS - it is the 17-point gap against the gross figure, not the level, that carries the return-rate signal.

metrics.name: Total Gross Sales (All Channels)
metrics.description: Gross sales across ALL channels including in-store. $1,178,971,663.73 all-time, tying exactly to the Retail Sales Activity model. Present only as the denominator for Digital Mix % - this model has no traffic or funnel data for in-store demand.

metrics.name: Digital Mix %
metrics.description: Digital Gross Sales / Total Gross Sales (All Channels). 25.19% all-time. Rising mix is the mechanism behind the company return rate worsening while every individual channel's return rate improves - see the Retail Omnichannel Fulfillment model.
